subject: Request: promo-credit stacking exception for MentorMatch mentor cohort
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@mentormatch.org>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: MentorMatch Finance <finance@mentormatch.org>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Promo stacking exception request for mentor cohort onboarding

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loves the latency and the per-token cost profile. We run a small nonprofit mentor cohort (MentorMatch’s Spring Mentor Fellowship) that onboards 120 mentors and a handful of partner orgs. Our partner sponsor has provided a $10k Redwood promo credit for onboarding and we also qualify for your standard "startup accelerator" onboarding credit (the $5k cohort sweetener).

Quick ask: can Redwood allow these two promo credits to be stacked for MentorMatch? Our finance/legal folks are concerned about workarounds in the contract and want written confirmation of the exception and any usage/expiry constraints. The cohort is onboarding next week (live tokens start 03/28) and we need clear billing guidance so we can finalize the OPO with our sponsor.

I attach the cohort mutual action plan and the sponsor acknowledgement (both short). If we can get a temporary exception (one-time stacking for this cohort) with milestone gating (e.g., credits only apply to onboarding tokens in the first 30 days), that would work for us.

Can you let me know the quickest way to get approval? Happy to hop on a 15-min call today if that helps.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Partnerships, MentorMatch
olivia@mentormatch.org

Attachments: MentorMatch_MAPlan_v3.pdf (doc), sponsor_acknowledgement.pdf (pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@mentormatch.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promo stacking exception request for mentor cohort onboarding

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the MAP. Looping in Marissa (sales lead for non-profit/cohort deals) and Irene (finance/legal ops) to evaluate.

High level: we prefer not to routinely stack externally-sponsored credits with program promos, but we do make one-off exceptions for accelerator/cohort programs when there is a clear mutual action plan and milestone gating. To move quickly, can you confirm: 1) Sponsor is okay with credits being applied only to onboarding-related usage in the first 30 days, 2) Sponsor contact for billing signoff (name+email), 3) whether MentorMatch requires any SOC2 or audit artifacts from Redwood for their procurement (Irene can advise).

If you can confirm the three items, Marissa and I will draft the exception memo (short addendum) and cut a one-time promo stacking token with explicit expiry and usage scope. If needed we can fast-track a signature via DocuSign.

Best,
Sean
Account Exec — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Promo stacking exception request for mentor cohort onboarding

Thanks Sean & Olivia — quick read-through here and proposed path:

Summary proposal (one-time exception)
- Grant: Stack sponsor $10k + Redwood cohort promo $5k = $15k total onboarding credit.
- Scope: Credits apply only to onboarding and integration-related usage tied to the MAP activities (API calls for mentor profiling, batch embedding jobs for the mentor dataset, and automated onboarding flows).
- Timebox: Credits valid for 30 days from first production request (we will anchor to the first token consumed in production).
- Controls: Credits will not apply to Dedicated capacity or private deploy fees. Any consumption outside scope will be billed at standard rates.
- Milestones & gating: Credits are unlocked in two tranches: 50% at first production token; remaining 50% released after MentorMatch completes the integration checklist in the MAP (itemized).
- Compliance ask: We need a short attestation from MentorMatch that they are a registered nonprofit (EIN or equivalent) and confirmation from the sponsor that stacking is acceptable. If MentorMatch requires SOC2 evidence, we can provide a SOC2-briefing packet (high level) but SOC2 attestation requires our security/legal review window — that could add 5–7 business days.

Attachments: I am attaching a draft exception memo (one-pager) and the SOC2 brief we usually send for procurement checks. If Olivia approves, Irene and I will finalize the addendum and route for an e-signature.

Next steps:
- Olivia: confirm sponsor billing contact + nonprofit attestation (EIN).
- Sean: confirm appetite to approve (Irene and I will wait for your go/no-go).

Olivia — we can issue the credits as promotional SKUs in HubSpot and attach the memo to the deal record. If MentorMatch absolutely needs the SOC2 report before signing, note the 5–7 day window above — otherwise we can proceed with the brief and an indemnity clause in the addendum.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_credits_exception_memo_draft.pdf (pdf), SOC2-briefing.pdf (pdf)

Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promo stacking exception request for mentor cohort onboarding — approval path

Quick update from finance & legal ops: we are comfortable approving the one-time stacking under the controls Marissa outlined with two minor edits: 1) add a clause that any credits not consumed within the 30-day window are forfeited (no rollover), and 2) require MentorMatch to confirm sponsor in writing (sponsor email + line stating they consent to stacking).

I will finalize the addendum text and attach it to the HubSpot deal. One operational note: to ensure clean accounting, we will create two separate promo SKUs (sponsor_applied_credit_MM and redwood_cohort_promo_MM) and mark the stacking exception in the line item memo. That keeps revenue recognition and sponsor reporting straightforward.

If Olivia can send the sponsor contact and the nonprofit EIN, I will push the addendum and the promo SKUs live today and Marissa can trigger issuance.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head, Finance & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
